subject: Recap: Discovery & buying criteria — Velotech Systems (procurement path & next steps)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Greene <alex.greene@velotech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Discovery & buying criteria — Velotech Systems (procurement path & next steps)

Hi Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and can move toward a procurement-ready plan. I’ve kept this short and action-oriented.

Summary of customer pain & goals (from today’s call)
- Pain: Frequent latency spikes on in-house embedding retrieval and expensive per-request token costs during batch analytics jobs.
- Goal: Reduce per-token cost for high-throughput search/QA by ~3x while keeping 95th percentile latency under 250ms for interactive flows.
- Non-negotiable: Data residency in US regions and full audit logs for queries.

Current stack / constraints
- Velotech uses an in-house microservice calling a mix of open checkpoints on NVidia A100s.
- Long-tail batch jobs run nightly on a different cluster; sensitive PII flows are routed to a separate data pipeline.

Success criteria (what a win looks like)
1) 3x reduction in token $/unit for embeddings+generation workload (measured over 30 days).
2) 95th percentile p99 latency below 250ms for the interactive path.
3) Audit logs + KMS-managed keys in US region.

Procurement & decision process (quick frame)
- Timeline: Velotech aiming for a vendor short-list by the end of August and a PO in September.
- Stakeholders you called out: Alex (Technical Sponsor), Procurement (formal approver), Samantha Lin (VP Product — executive sponsor), and Legal (TBD).
- Typical procurement path we’ve seen for similar customers: Technical evaluation (2–3 weeks) -> Security questionnaires + SOC 2 artifacts -> Commercial term negotiation -> PO.

Preliminary commercial guardrails (for planning only)
- Targeted annual committed spend range we think will fit given your volume: $150k–$450k. This is a placeholder for sizing conversation; we can tighten after workload telemetry.
- Desired billing term: monthly with an option to convert to annual committed capacity for discounts.

Next steps (proposed)
1) I’ll share a short scoping spreadsheet (attached) that captures peak concurrency, token distribution, and PII routing — please ask your infra lead to fill the grey cells. (Attachment: redwood_scoping_sheet.xlsx)
2) Procurement: Alex, can we get the name/email of the procurement contact and any internal RFP deadline?
3) Technical: propose a 45-minute technical validation call week of Jul 27 to walk a quick integration test and latency baseline.
4) We’ll surface SOC 2 + security artifacts immediately and flag any contractual constraints that could affect timeline.

Attachments: redwood_scoping_sheet.xlsx, meeting-recording-20260722.mp4

If that captures your view, I’ll loop in our security lead and your procurement contact and propose the technical slot.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

---
(Internal note) cc: Marissa — would like you to weigh in on commercial guardrails and whether we should surface an initial MPS pricing range in the technical call.

Subject: Re: Recap: Discovery & buying criteria — Velotech Systems (procurement path & next steps)

Thanks, Karthik — this is very helpful and aligns with my notes. A couple quick clarifications: 

- Procurement contact is Tara Mullins (procure@velotech.com). RFP deadline is targeted for 2026-08-25.
- Our legal will likely require a vendor security review; SOC 2 + network diagram will be mandatory.
- Samantha is available for a 30-min executive sponsor call the week of Aug 2 — prefer Aug 4 in the morning PST.

I've attached the RFP outline we use internally; it lists mandatory items and evaluation criteria. I’ll ask Tara to confirm the RFP timeline formally.

Attachment: Velotech_RFP.pdf

On the budget band — $150k–$450k seems doable to get us into the pilot conversation. We’ll need a clearer per-token estimate for the interactive path and an option for a short-term pilot without long-term committal.

On the technical call: please include your security lead and someone who can speak to caching/quantization options.

Appreciate the concise framing.

—Alex

alex.greene@velotech.com | +1 206-555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Greene <alex.greene@velotech.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Velotech Procurement <procure@velotech.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Discovery & buying criteria — Velotech Systems (procurement path & next steps)

Alex — looping in a couple of quick commercial guardrails to help procurement scope a pilot vs committed option. Short bullets so Tara/Procurement can act quickly: 

- Pilot option (preferred for initial validation): 8–10 week pilot with usage-based billing, capped spend not to exceed $35k for the pilot period. Pilot includes standard support (email + ticketing) and a single engineering office hours slot per week.
- Committed option: 12-month committed capacity with tiered pricing. For the mid-level workload signals you described, typical committed deals start at $150k annual and include discounted token rates, dedicated routing policy, and SLO targets (SLA 99.9% uptime for API).
- Security & Legal: Redwood can provide SOC 2 Type II report, network diagram, and data processing addendum (DPA). Karthik will share the scoping sheet and we can push the security artifacts to your security mailbox immediately.

Karthik — I’d recommend offering the pilot as the default next step in the technical call; it shortens procurement friction and lets us produce measured telemetry to firm up pricing. If Tara prefers an annual commit, we’ll map to a committed-capacity proposal with a clear PO path.

Action items
- Tara: please confirm who from Legal should receive SOC 2 and the DPA (email for delivery).
- Alex: confirm executive sponsor availability (Aug 4 morning PST is proposed).
- Karthik: send the scoping sheet link and propose 2 slots for the technical validation call next week.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
